rationale: The target correctly represents the standard-normal absolute L^p moment as the 1/p real power of the integral of |x|^p under gaussianReal 0 1, with a p-independent positive constant and square-root growth. All 36 dependencies have their intended effect, including Real.rpow, the Bochner integral, real absolute value, and the Gaussian measure. The only substantive difference is quantifier strength: (2.11) is eventual as p tends to infinity, whereas Lean requires the bound for every real p >= 1. That added bounded-range obligation is meaningful and nonvacuous, so Lean implies the source but the selected numbered source assertion does not conversely imply Lean. The resulting accepted classification is faithful-stronger, with no unresolved evidence or ambiguity requiring adjudication.
